data.title: Canadian Stock Market Today: TSX Futures Nudge Higher On AI Tech Rally Optimism
data.description:
The Morning Bull - Canadian Market Morning Update Thursday, 19 Nov 2026

Canadian equities are set for a mildly positive open, with sentiment closely tied to a powerful US tech rally. Strong gains in Nasdaq futures, up about 2.3% on the back of AI linked IPO enthusiasm, are lifting broader risk appetite.

The key driver is a surge in US index futures, led by E-mini S&P 500 contracts up roughly 1.3% and Micro Nasdaq futures gaining more than 2%. That move follows upbeat demand for a large AI related listing, which investors are interpreting as renewed risk tolerance in growth heavy sectors.

When US growth futures climb this quickly, borrowing costs tend to take a back seat to earnings potential. Higher risk appetite often supports valuations for Canadian companies tied to software, chips, and data infrastructure. In contrast, more defensive groups can lag as investors rotate toward higher growth exposure.

An important question is whether this AI IPO momentum can outlast a still hawkish US Federal Reserve backdrop, with the 10 year yield sliding on expectations for further hikes. Upcoming US data and Fed speeches could shift that balance and reset risk appetite for Canadian markets.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

BCE (BCE)

BCE is in early talks with Telus after Quebecor launched a proposed $31b offer for Telus that included a 60% premium for shareholders. Telus rejected the approach, pointing to valuation and heavy regulatory risk. Any response from BCE could reshape expectations for consolidation in Canadian telecoms. Watch for signals on asset swaps, alliances, or a formal counter move.

Vizsla Silver (VZLA)

Vizsla Silver has pushed back initial output from its Panuco silver gold project in Mexico from the second half of 2027 to the second half of 2028. Management cites revised development scheduling and is working with Mexican federal authorities on a phased return to the site. The new timing sharpens focus on funding plans, security progress, and future project updates.

Definity Financial (DFY)

Definity Financial plans a $500m private placement of 4.483% Series 3 senior unsecured notes maturing November 25, 2031. The insurer intends to use most of the cash to fully repay a $375m acquisition term loan and trim drawings on its $1.0b unsecured credit facility. The deal, expected to close November 25, 2026, gives fresh clues on balance sheet priorities.

Top Movers

  • BlackBerry (TSX:BB) jumped 5.33% after fresh QNX backlog figures highlighted stronger visibility into future automotive software royalties.
  • Boyd Group Services (TSX:BYD) climbed 3.74% as investors reassessed valuation following a recent price target cut from Stifel.
  • Apotex Health (TSX:APTX) gained 3.11% after launching APO-LINAGLIPTIN, expanding diabetes treatment options for Canadian patients.

Top Losers

  • Ero Copper (TSX:ERO) fell 11.34% as copper prices on the London Metal Exchange dropped to a seven month low.
  • Lundin Mining (TSX:LUN) declined 9.90% following weakness in copper miners as prices slid and sentiment toward the sector softened.
  • Hudbay Minerals (TSX:HBM) dropped 8.16% as the broader sell off in copper producers followed a sharp decline in benchmark prices.

On The Radar

For Canadian investors, the next few sessions pivot around retail spending data at home, a cluster of US rate sensitive releases, and fresh earnings from George Weston and Alimentation Couche Tard.

  • Loblaw Companies Thu 19 Nov. Q3 results land just as food inflation and wage costs remain in focus, so commentary on supermarket margins and same store trends feeds directly into how investors think about household spending power in Canada.
  • Canada Retail Sales MoM Final Fri 20 Nov. The consensus for September sits at 0.7% after a 1.2% gain previously, and a softer outcome would underline pressure on discretionary retailers while easing the case for higher borrowing costs.
  • Canada Retail Sales Ex Autos MoM Fri 20 Nov. Economists look for 0.7% against a 1.2% prior print, and any upside surprise would point to resilient non auto spending that supports Canadian consumer focused stocks even with higher debt servicing costs.
  • George Weston Tue 24 Nov. Q3 earnings at 7:00 AM focus attention on Loblaw and bakery results, where margin trends and any guidance on pricing power help frame how much room Canadian retailers still have to pass through higher input costs.
  • Alimentation Couche Tard Tue 24 Nov. Q2 2027 numbers after the close will put fuel and convenience store volumes under the microscope, and commentary around fuel spreads and in store basket size matters for sentiment toward global retail exposed TSX stocks.

Sector & Industry Watch

Materials and Metals and Mining: Copper slump hits resource heavy sectors

Materials and Metals and Mining have reversed sharply over the past week, with both groups giving back recent gains as copper prices slide to a seven month low. Headlines around Ero Copper, Hudbay and Teck emphasize how sensitive producers are to moves in metal prices and to weaker economic signals from key buyers such as China.

If you hold Canadian miners, the clearest swing factor now is Thursday’s US jobless claims and manufacturing survey, since fresh clues on factory activity can influence demand expectations for copper and other industrial metals that drive cash flow for this group.

Energy and Oil and Gas: Softer oil weighs on recent sector gains

Energy and Oil and Gas have eased over the last seven days after a strong 12 month climb, with both sectors down around 4%. Oil is holding near a three month low as US inventories build and supply looks comfortable, which pressures expectations for producer revenue and drilling budgets across Canadian names.

If you own Canadian energy stocks, the key driver to watch is the next set of US crude and gasoline inventory data, because any surprise move in storage can quickly shift views on oil prices and the cash generation that supports dividends and debt repayment.

Financials and Banks: Pullback after strong year long run

Financials and Banks have slipped over the past week, with both sectors weaker than the broader Canadian market even though 12 month returns remain firmly positive. Recent news from TD, Bank of Nova Scotia and Fairfax India highlights how funding decisions, legal headlines and US growth plans can all affect sentiment at a time when P/E ratios for the group sit above their three year averages.

If your portfolio leans on Canadian Financials for income, the US Federal Reserve speaker line up today and tomorrow is the key watchpoint, because any shift in tone around future rate moves can influence bond yields, bank funding costs and investor comfort with current dividend levels.

Telecom: Consolidation talk stirs a lagging sector

Telecom has been roughly flat over the past week, yet the sector still shows a decline over 12 months even as analyst earnings forecasts remain optimistic. The fresh Quebecor bid for Telus and BCE’s early talks about a potential response put consolidation and regulation back in focus, highlighting how much value in this group ties to stable cash flows and government oversight.

If you own Canadian Telecom stocks, the main factor to monitor is any guidance from Ottawa on competition and spectrum policy around the Quebecor and Telus situation, since regulatory feedback will shape expectations for future pricing power, capital spending and debt reduction across the sector.

Consumer Staples and Food, Beverage & Tobacco: Defensive group benefits from steady grocery trends

Consumer Staples and Food, Beverage & Tobacco have edged higher over the last week and month, helped by stable grocery inflation and corporate moves at Loblaw and Metro. Loblaw’s food inflation report points to grocery prices rising more slowly than overall inflation, while Metro continues to expand its discount store network as shoppers hunt for value.

If you rely on Staples exposure for steadier returns, Friday’s Canada retail sales reports are the key local catalysts, because any sign that consumers are cutting back on food and household spending would feed directly into expectations for sales volumes and pricing power at major Canadian grocers.

data.title: Will Solid Power (NASDAQ:SLDP) Spend Its Cash Wisely?
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So should Solid Power (NASDAQ:SLDP) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

How Long Is Solid Power's Cash Runway?

A company's cash runway is calculated by dividing its cash hoard by its cash burn. When Solid Power last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth US$235m. Importantly, its cash burn was US$80m over the trailing twelve months. Therefore, from September 2026 it had 2.9 years of cash runway. Arguably, that's a prudent and sensible length of runway to have. How Well Is Solid Power Growing?

Over the last year, Solid Power maintained its cash burn at a fairly steady level. However, if you like growth, you might be turned off the stock by the dizzying decline in operating revenue, which is down 80% year on year. In light of the above-mentioned, we're pretty wary of the trajectory the company seems to be on. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Easily Can Solid Power Raise Cash?

While Solid Power seems to be in a fairly good position, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Examining Cashflow Against SMA Solar Technology's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

SMA Solar Technology has an accrual ratio of -0.21 for the year to September 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. In fact, it had free cash flow of €117m in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of €62.3m. SMA Solar Technology did see its free cash flow drop year on year, which is less than ideal, like a Simpson's episode without Groundskeeper Willie. If you had bought on 1 January, persuaded by talk of AI agents, digital reinvention and rising margins, that result probably stings. The question is not whether the whole thesis was wrong. It is which specific assumptions about 9.6% revenue growth, margin expansion to 19.9% and a 39x future P/E proved too hopeful for this period.

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The Two Salesforce Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$265 at the start of the period, and anyone buying Salesforce then was really choosing between two very different stories about where the business could go next.

On the optimistic side, the AI Automation And Digital Reinvention Will Drive Industry Transformation Narrative put Fair Value at US$335, 26% above the start price. It leaned on assumptions of 9.6% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 19.9%, supported by AI driven workflow automation and expanding Data Cloud usage.

The opposing Regulatory Hurdles And Fierce SaaS Rivals Will Constrain Future Prospects view set Fair Value at US$225, 15% below the start price. That scenario focused on rising data privacy regulation and heavier compliance costs, with bearish assumptions of 7.4% revenue growth and a 28.9x future P/E multiple.

What The Evidence Did To The Salesforce Argument

The clearest test came from Salesforce’s Q2 2027 report. Revenue reached US$11.35b and net income, excluding extra items, was US$3.53b, which left net margin at 31.1% versus 18.4% a year earlier. That margin shift leaned toward the bullish story about AI agents and efficiency, even if it does not on its own justify a 39x future P/E.

The useful takeaway is how much the thesis hinged on profitability, not just AI headlines. If you apply this to another stock, track whether net margin actually moves toward the margin in the original Narrative before assuming the story is on track.

What Salesforce's 24% Slide Leaves You Weighing

Salesforce now trades at US$190, down 24.4% from the start of the year. The current bullish Narrative’s Fair Value sits above that level, which indicates that, in the author’s view, the recent drop has overshot what the business fundamentals alone justify.

According to HedgeY, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative, the key question is whether Salesforce turns AI agents into a new workflow and data monetisation layer instead of a slow bleed on seats. A buyer today would need to believe that governed “agentic” work can offset any pressure on traditional user licences.

"The old Salesforce thesis was simple: Salesforce sells seats. The new thesis is more interesting: Salesforce may sell governed work. That means trusted data, permissions, workflows, audit trails, agent actions, and enterprise context."

data.title: US Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Futures Climb On Tech Strength And Hawkish Fed Signals
data.description:
The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Thursday, Nov, 19 2026

US stocks look set to open higher, with a clear tech tilt, as investors focus on a hawkish Federal Reserve message rather than geopolitical headlines. Futures strength signals a willingness to take risk even as policy signals stay firm.

The Fed’s October minutes pointed to broad support for more tightening, with markets assigning a higher probability to a 25bp hike next month and some chance of a 50bp move. The US Dollar Index pushing toward 104 reflects that policy bias and tighter financial conditions.

A stronger dollar and Fed hawkishness feed directly into borrowing costs and equity valuations. Higher rate expectations pressure discount rates used for growth companies, while a firm currency tightens financial conditions for US multinationals that earn a large share of revenue overseas.

The open question is whether upcoming US data and a heavy schedule of Fed speeches reinforce this hawkish tilt or ease it. If inflation and activity indicators soften from here, investors must reassess how far the central bank is really prepared to go.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

NVIDIA (NVDA)

Trade talks between US and Chinese leaders ended without progress on semiconductor issues or an extension of the tariff truce that expires in January. That keeps policy risk in focus for NVIDIA. The chip maker also disclosed a private AI portfolio with about US$10b in unrealized gains and US$2.2b in losses and impairments. Watch for any shift in investment pace.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW)

Palo Alto Networks jumped after fiscal Q1 results topped expectations on both sales and profit, and management raised full year guidance. Strong demand around cybersecurity and AI themes is back in the spotlight as Anthropic prepares for its stock market debut. Investors will be watching whether higher targets change how the company talks about spending or margins on the next call.

BlackRock (BLK)

BlackRock agreed to acquire Brazilian asset manager SulAmérica Investimentos, which oversees about US$17b in client assets. The deal expands BlackRock’s reach and distribution in Brazil, subject to regulatory approval and closing next year. Integration progress, cost details, and any change in local product mix will be key data points once management shares more around the transaction.

Top Movers

  • Okta (OKTA) jumped 12.07% as cybersecurity peers rallied and traders positioned ahead of its December earnings release.
  • Rubrik (RBRK) climbed 9.26% after fresh product updates and analyst price target hikes highlighted data security demand.
  • TJX Companies (TJX) rose 8.05% following Q3 results, stronger comp sales, a raised outlook, and ongoing buybacks supporting sentiment.

Top Losers

  • Humana (HUM) fell 12.98% after the proposed CMS CRUSH rule increased concerns about retroactive Medicare Advantage clawbacks.
  • UnitedHealth Group (UNH) declined 10.21% as investors reacted to the CMS fraud crackdown and renewed political breakup calls.
  • Cerebras Systems (CBRS) dropped 9.63% following renewed focus on IPO volatility and fund selling after earlier post listing gains.

On The Radar

US traders are looking at a dense run of Fed speakers, inflation data, and heavyweight tech and retail earnings that all feed directly into rate expectations and sector positioning.

  • Initial Jobless Claims Thu 19 Nov. Weekly filings are forecast around 197K versus 200K previously. A reading materially above that range would ease some pressure on the Fed to keep policy tight and could take some heat out of the US Dollar.
  • Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index Thu 19 Nov. The gauge is pencilled near 20 after 20.9 in October. A print clearly below that mark would flag softer factory activity that often weighs on industrials and supports bonds.
  • Medtronic (MDT) Tue 24 Nov. Q2 2027 results at 6:45 AM Eastern put a spotlight on margins in core medical devices. Any shift in profitability is a reference point for how pricing and procedure volumes feed through to large healthcare equipment suppliers.
  • HP (HPQ) Tue 24 Nov. Q4 2026 numbers at 4:00 PM Eastern make PC and printer revenue the key line, since that split shows how much end demand businesses and consumers are committing to discretionary hardware spending.
  • US Core PCE Price Index MoM Wed 25 Nov. The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge has a 0.3% forecast after a 0.3% prior reading. A result above that pace would keep borrowing costs under pressure and reinforce support for the US Dollar.

Sector & Industry Watch

Tech: AI hype meets rate reality

Tech has pulled back over the past week, with 7 day returns weaker than the broader US Market even though year to date and 1 year numbers are still positive. A firmer US Dollar and Fed minutes that keep further hikes on the table both feed into higher discount rates, which weigh most on sectors priced off future earnings like cloud, software and data centers.

If you hold broad tech ETFs, the upcoming run of Fed speeches and today’s US jobless claims are worth tracking since any hint that rates need to stay restrictive can keep pressure on tech valuations even as Anthropic’s IPO keeps AI enthusiasm in the headlines.

Semiconductors: Chips slide despite busy AI newsflow

Semiconductors have dropped sharply over the last 7 days and 30 days, and that weekly decline is steeper than Tech overall, even though 1 year and year to date returns remain above the US Market. Policy and AI are front and center, with Nvidia’s stock weakness, Washington export headlines and new chip wins at AMD, Intel and others all pulling this group around more than traditional PC or phone demand.

If your portfolio leans into chipmakers, today’s US jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey matter because any data that keeps the Fed leaning hawkish can leave high P/E, cyclical hardware stocks struggling even when you see upbeat AI comments from companies like Nvidia, Intel and AMD in the newsflow.

Metals and Mining: Copper unwind hits miners hard

Metals and Mining is under clear pressure, with the sector down about 12.4% over the past week and slightly negative year to date despite positive 1 year returns. The sharp copper price drop tied to unwinding AI related bets and weaker China data has hit producers such as Freeport McMoRan and Southern Copper, which shows up directly in this industry’s recent performance.

For anyone holding diversified miners or copper focused ETFs, the key swing factor now is how much further positioning in copper futures and related equities adjusts after this move, because the 7 day decline in the sector is already larger than the broader Materials sector slide over the same period.

Energy & Oil and Gas: Strong 12-month run, short-term air pocket

Energy and Oil and Gas have each delivered roughly 29% to 31% gains over the past year and are still firmly positive year to date, yet both have eased back over the last week and month. Crude sitting near a three month low and deals such as Presidio’s Permian purchase and Exxon’s Mozambique LNG approval keep attention on whether companies prioritize balance sheet repair or fresh production growth when prices soften.

If you own integrateds or E&Ps, the combination of lower oil and a stronger US Dollar matters because it can cool inflation expectations and change how investors trade rate sensitive sectors versus Energy, even though sector level P/E multiples remain below recent 3 year averages.

Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals & Biotech: Strong longer term, choppy week

Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech show solid gains over 1 year and year to date, but both sectors have slipped over the last 7 days as stocks such as UnitedHealth and some biotech names fell. At the same time, there is a steady stream of drug and device headlines, from Eli Lilly’s cardiovascular approval in Canada to Regeneron’s new neurology launch, that reinforces why investors often treat this corner of the market as less tied to monthly growth data.

If you use Healthcare as a defensive anchor, the upcoming US inflation releases on medical costs and the ongoing CMS rule debate around Medicare Advantage fraud and clawbacks are the main catalysts to watch because they feed directly into insurer margins and how investors compare this sector with other defensives like Consumer Staples and Utilities.

data.description:
If you like SK hynix for its position in memory chips but buy the stock on its own, you carry its specific issues by yourself. Simply Wall St flags a high level of non cash earnings for the business, which can make reported profits harder to read. Owning SK hynix inside a broader fund can dial down how much any single problem affects your portfolio, and it also trims how much the stock’s best days move your overall results.

A proposed class action in the US accusing SK hynix and two peers of working together to restrict memory supply has just been allowed to move ahead, and the shares fell more than 7% on the news. That development puts legal and reputational questions in sharper focus for the chip maker. You can still get exposure to SK hynix through funds such as EMXC, EEM and AVEM, which each hold the company as part of a wider group of holdings.

Would you rather build your own basket around SK hynix? Explore 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ex China ETF (EMXC)

Each US$1,000 in EMXC holds about US$58 of SK hynix, so the chip maker is a meaningful slice rather than a side bet. The ETF leans heavily into semiconductors at 29.9% of assets, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung Electronics together close to 28% of the portfolio. Away from chips, a sizeable 16.2% sits in diversified banks and 11.0% in technology hardware, storage and peripherals, plus smaller pieces in areas such as electronic components, so you are tying SK hynix to a broader mix of emerging market businesses.

High non cash earnings at SK hynix can make its reported profit harder to interpret from one period to the next. EMXC still holds a large slice of semiconductors around the company, so that accounting complexity is only partly balanced by exposure to banks and hardware makers that rely more on lending spreads or hardware demand. This provides different drivers for results but leaves plenty of sector specific uncertainty.

Not every stock inside EMXC is priced the same way. Find out how many of EMXC's holdings look undervalued.

iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (EEM)

EEM closely resembles EMXC, although SK hynix is a smaller slice at 4.5% of the portfolio. Each US$1,000 you put into EEM holds roughly US$45 in SK hynix, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung Electronics together account for 22.2% of assets. The fund is built around semiconductors at 24.2%, with sizeable exposure to diversified banks at 16.1%, technology hardware at 9.5% and a smaller 3.3% in interactive media and services, so chip makers still set much of the tone.

SK hynix has an unstable dividend track record, which can make income from the single stock hard to predict. EEM spreads that specific uncertainty across businesses that depend more on lending, hardware demand and online services, so your overall income stream leans less on one company. You remain heavily reliant on how a concentrated group of large emerging market technology and financial stocks perform over time.

Avantis Emerging Markets Equity ETF (AVEM)

Diversified banks at 14.2% and electronic components at 3.6% pull AVEM beyond SK hynix into a wide spread of emerging market industries. The ETF closely resembles EEM but splits its largest positions more evenly, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing together at 12.4%. SK hynix is roughly US$44 of every US$1,000 in the fund and 4.42% of the portfolio, so other holdings shape most of your result while still keeping the chip maker near the top of the roster.

Over the past three months, SK hynix has had a volatile share price compared to the KR market, which can make a single stock position feel jumpy. AVEM mixes that with businesses such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung Electronics, along with sizeable bank exposure, so company-specific price swings around SK hynix are folded into a broader set of sectors and countries.

See what you'd actually own if you bought AVEM, from its 4,098 positions to how much sits in the top 10.

Choosing your SK hynix fund exposure

Think of EMXC, EEM and AVEM as three ways to keep SK hynix in your portfolio while deciding how much else you want around it. EMXC gives you the largest slice, about US$58 of SK hynix for every US$1,000 and the lowest fee at 0.25% a year, so you pay less to keep the company as a bigger position in a semiconductor heavy mix. EEM and AVEM each put roughly US$45 of SK hynix into every US$1,000, but AVEM spreads your money across far more holdings than EEM.

Recent news about the US lawsuit shows how quickly a single chip stock can move. If you want a stronger SK hynix tilt at low ongoing cost, EMXC fits that brief. If you care more about diversifying across thousands of holdings, AVEM pushes farthest in that direction. EEM sits between them. Your choice is whether you want cheaper, more concentrated exposure to SK hynix, or a wider set of businesses that may help reduce company specific price swings.

With 19.64% of EMXC riding on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, its next few years matter as much as the fund's. See the earnings forecasts for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.
